robertsFlores.title: About the algorithm
robertsFlores.paragraph1: Roberts-Flores Algorithm is a method for finding all Hamiltonian cycles in a graph using backtracking.
robertsFlores.paragraph2: The algorithm systematically builds all possible paths starting from the initial vertex and checks if they form a Hamiltonian cycle.
robertsFlores.tip: 💡 Tip: For best results, use a connected graph with 4-7 vertices.

prim.title: About the algorithm
prim.paragraph1: Prim's Algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by gradually expanding the spanning tree with vertices through the edge of minimum weight.
prim.paragraph2: Works with an undirected weighted graph without negative weights.
prim.tip: 💡 Tip: Use a symmetric matrix with weights > 0. Diagonal — 0.

bellmanFord.title: About the algorithm
bellmanFord.paragraph1: Bellman-Ford Algorithm is an algorithm for finding shortest paths from one vertex to all others in a directed weighted graph. Unlike Dijkstra's algorithm, it can work with edges of negative weight and detect negative cycles.
bellmanFord.paragraph2: The algorithm performs V-1 iterations of relaxation of all edges, where V is the number of vertices. After that, an additional check is performed for the presence of negative cycles.
bellmanFord.paragraph3: Time complexity: O(V × E), where V is the number of vertices, E is the number of edges.
bellmanFord.tip: 💡 Tip: Use a weight matrix where element [i][j] is the weight of the edge from vertex i to vertex j. Use 0 for no edge or 'inf' for infinity.

hungarian.title: About the algorithm
hungarian.paragraph1: Hungarian Algorithm is an algorithm for solving the assignment problem, which consists of finding the optimal assignment of elements of one set to elements of another set with minimal total cost.
hungarian.paragraph2: The algorithm works with a square cost matrix and finds such an assignment where each element of the first set is assigned to exactly one element of the second set, and the total cost is minimal.
hungarian.paragraph3: Time complexity: O(n³), where n is the size of the matrix.
hungarian.tip: 💡 Tip: Use a square cost matrix. The graph will be represented as a bipartite graph, where the left part is sources, the right part is targets.

graphColoring.title: About the algorithm
graphColoring.paragraph1: Graph Coloring Algorithm is an algorithm for assigning colors to graph vertices such that no two adjacent vertices have the same color.
graphColoring.paragraph2: A greedy algorithm (Greedy Coloring) is implemented, which goes through vertices and assigns each vertex the minimum available color (not used by its neighbors).
graphColoring.paragraph3: The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colors needed for proper coloring. The greedy algorithm does not always find the optimal solution, but works quickly.
graphColoring.tip: 💡 Tip: The algorithm works with undirected graphs. The matrix must be symmetric.

bronKerbosch.title: About the algorithm
bronKerbosch.paragraph1: Bron-Kerbosch Algorithm is an algorithm for finding all maximal cliques in an undirected graph using the backtracking method.
bronKerbosch.paragraph2: A clique is a subset of graph vertices in which every pair of vertices is connected by an edge. A maximal clique is a clique that cannot be expanded by adding another vertex.
bronKerbosch.paragraph3: The algorithm uses three sets: R (current clique), P (candidates for addition), and X (excluded vertices).
bronKerbosch.tip: 💡 Tip: The algorithm works only with undirected graphs. The matrix must be symmetric.
